messages.subject: D-RUG and Tea Time this Thursday!
messages.subject_clean: D-RUG and Tea Time this Thursday!
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGgies!

We will be meeting this Thursday (5/8) from 10-noon virtually and in person in the DataLab classroom (Library 360). This is a group working session so come with your questions for our expeRts, or just bring your laptop and get in some distraction free R-coding time. Additionally, if there are topics you would like to see someone do a deeper dive on, let us know!

Datalab will also be open for Tea Time on Thursday afternoon as well.

D-RUG: 10am-noon, DataLab Classroom, Library 360, and zoom https://ucdavis.zoom.us/j/96397082218?pwd=S0JXcW5hcUFkbTcwMHFQV1NVNkg3Zz09
Tea Time: 1-2pm, DataLab Classroom, Library 360

Please consider posting your questions to our Discourse <https://d-rug.discourse.group/> site in advance of attending D-RUG virtually. This helps us do a better job of answering your questions, and also keep a log of the types of questions we see frequently.

See you then,

Your D-RUG Coo[R]dinators

messages.subject: FW: [opensource-announce] Collaborate and Grow: Open Source for Research Coders
messages.subject_clean: [opensource-announce] Collaborate and Grow: Open Source for Research Coders
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

As R users, you all are members of a broader group of open-source software users. The event below can help you build connections with that community in academia and beyond. And if nothing else you can hang out with me!

-Elise

--

Elise Hellwig

Research Data Scientist, she/her

UC Davis DataLab: Data Science and Informatics

eche...@ucdavis.edu, 370 Shields Library

From: opensource-announce Sympa List (request) <opensource-an...@ucdavis.edu> on behalf of Laura Langdon <lala...@ucdavis.edu>
Date: Wednesday, May 14, 2025 at 4:42 PM
To: opensource-announce Sympa List <opensourc...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: Re: [opensource-announce] Collaborate and Grow: Open Source for Research Coders

Sorry, that should have said “Thursday, May 29”!

From: opensource-an...@ucdavis.edu <opensource-an...@ucdavis.edu> on behalf of lala...@ucdavis.edu <lala...@ucdavis.edu>
Date: Wednesday, May 14, 2025 at 4:39 PM
To: opensource-announce Sympa List <opensourc...@ucdavis.edu>
Subject: [opensource-announce] Collaborate and Grow: Open Source for Research Coders

Are you a researcher or student who writes scripts, handles data, or maintains
specialized tools? Without realizing it, you might already be part of the open
source community! This casual one-hour gathering is designed specifically for
scientists, researchers, and academics who code as part of their work but
might not necessarily identify as "programmers."

Whether you're a biologist analyzing genomic data, a sociologist processing
survey results, or a geologist mapping terrain features, this meetup will show
you how your coding skills connect to the broader open source ecosystem. We'll
explore how the tools you already use (and perhaps contribute to) fit into the
open source landscape, and discuss simple ways to benefit from and participate
in this collaborative community.

Join us Thursday, May 27 at 3pm for refreshments and conversation with others
who, like you, use computation to advance their research. No technical
expertise required—just register below and bring your curiosity!

Registration:
https://events.library.ucdavis.edu/event/open-source-meetup-may-2025

See you there!

- The UC Davis OSPO

messages.subject: Call for Instructors - Teach a GeoSpatial Workshop in Fall 2025
messages.subject_clean: Call for Instructors - Teach a GeoSpatial Workshop in Fall 2025
messages.body_plain:
My two cents: BayGeo is great to work with! That Intro to QGIS workshop we teach at maptimeDavis was something I originally developed for BayGeo many years ago. See the call for instructors below.

---

BayGeo <https://www.baygeo.org/> is looking for instructors to teach geospatial workshops this Fall (late August through December). Our workshops are like short courses, typically meeting once per week for a few hours, for a few consecutive weeks. The workshops are geared toward working professionals. Topics can cover anything geospatial, and this year we're especially in need of someone to teach spatial R.

Workshops can be held virtually (Zoom) or in-person using the GIS lab at the University of San Francisco. Instructors are paid $75/hour of instruction, plus some additional paid hours for prep.

BayGeo is a non-profit organization with a mission to foster a vibrant geospatial community by facilitating knowledge sharing, networking, and professional development in the SF Bay Area and beyond!

If you're interested in teaching a workshop, contact Cam Denney at cde...@baygeo.org

Michele Tobias, PhD

Geospatial Data Scientist

DataLab: Data Science & Informatics

UC Davis Library

370 Shields Library

(530)752-7532

mmto...@ucdavis.edu

ORCID: 0000-0002-2954-8710 <https://orcid.org/0000-0002-2954-8710>

Pronouns: she, her, hers

messages.subject: HPC (Farm, Hive, Peloton) Offline 6/16 - 6/20
messages.body_plain:
Hi D-RUGies!

The HPC will be running it's biannual maintenance from Monday, June 16th to Friday, June 20th, during which time Farm, Hive, and Peloton will be completely offline. Any jobs running on 6/16 will be killed and will need to be restarted after the maintenance window.

Cheers,
Elise
